questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The term 'accounting period' is used to refer to the
options: time span during which taxes are paid to the Inland Revenue Board
budget period, usually one year, relied on by the accountant
time span, usually one year, covered by financial statements
period within which debtors are expected to settle accounts
questions.explanation: The accounting period is the span of time (usually a year) that a set of financial statements covers.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Assigning revenues to the accounting period in which goods were sold or services rendered and expenses incurred is known as
questions.explanation: The matching concept matches revenues with the expenses incurred to earn them in the same period.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The accounting convention which states that 'profit must not be recognized until realized while all losses should be adequately provided for' is termed
questions.explanation: Conservatism (prudence) anticipates no profit but provides for all possible losses.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Accounting information is used by investors and creditors of a company to predict
options: future cash flows of the company
future tax payments of the company
potential merger candidates for the company
appropriate remuneration for the company's staff
questions.explanation: Investors and creditors use accounting information to assess the amount and timing of future cash flows.

questions.stem: Antics Electronics Company recently bought six generators. Which of the following is the correct method of recording this transaction?
options: Debit generator account and credit cash account.
Debit purchases account and credit cash account.
Debit cash account and credit purchases account.
Debit cash account and credit generator account.
questions.explanation: Generators bought for use are fixed assets: debit the asset (generator) account, credit cash which was given out.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: When a business incurs labour cost in installing a fixed asset, the cost is treated as
questions.explanation: Costs of getting a fixed asset ready for use, such as installation labour, are capitalised as part of the asset's cost.

questions.stem: What is the cardinal rule of the double entry system?
options: Debit the increasing account and credit the decreasing account.
Debit the receiving account and credit the giving account.
Debit the asset account and credit the liability account.
Debit the revenue account and credit the expenditure account.
questions.explanation: The basic double-entry rule is to debit the account that receives value and credit the account that gives value.

questions.stem: Malam Gambo bought a freezer for his shop costing N10,500. In recording, he debited office expenses account and credited the bank account. What book keeping error has he committed?
questions.explanation: Posting a capital item (a fixed asset) to a revenue expense account is an error of principle.

questions.stem: The use of the folio in the ledger is for
questions.explanation: The folio column cross-references entries to the page of the book where the other entry is found.

questions.stem:
Account of Tanko Nig Ltd.
Dr: 1/10 Bal. b/f N5,000; Sales N10,000
Cr: 2/10 Cash N3,000; 15/10 Bank N6,500
What is the closing balance of the account shown above?
questions.explanation: Debits total N15,000 and credits total N9,500, so the balance is N5,500 (debit).

questions.stem: The suspense account is used to correct book keeping errors where the
options: error does not affect the agreement of the trial balance
questions.explanation: A suspense account temporarily holds a trial balance difference whose cause (the item involved) is not yet known.

questions.stem: The discount column of a three column cashbook is not balanced off but periodically transferred to the discount accounts because discounts
options: are not important in cash book
do not form part of double entry
questions.explanation: The discount columns are memorandum columns, not part of the double entry, so their totals are posted to the discount accounts.

questions.stem: When is a petty cash account debited?
options: When the fund is established and every time money is spent
When the fund is established and every time it is replenished
When the fund is established and when the size of the float is decreased
Every time money is drawn from the petty cash
questions.explanation: Petty cash is debited with the original float and with each reimbursement under the imprest system.

questions.stem: When preparing a bank reconciliation statement, which of the following is deducted from the balance per bank statement?
questions.explanation: Cheques issued but not yet presented have not reduced the bank statement balance, so they are deducted from it.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The financial position of an organization at a particular time can be ascertained from the
options: statement of sources and application of funds
questions.explanation: The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and capital at a particular date.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given: Purchases N20,000; Sales N40,000; Carriage inwards N5,000; Carriage outwards N5,000; Opening stock N10,000; Closing stock N5,000. What is the cost of goods sold?
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold = 10,000 + 20,000 + 5,000 (carriage inwards) - 5,000 = N30,000; carriage outwards is a selling expense.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The net profit or loss for the year is determined in the profit and loss account after
options: deducting cost of goods sold from sales and adding administrative expenses
adding commissions received to gross profit
eliminating all expenses from gross profit and adding any other income
questions.explanation: Net profit = gross profit + other income - all expenses.

questions.stem:
Use the table: Opening balance 1/1/90: 3,000 units at N3.00; Purchases January: 15,000 units at N3.50; Purchases February: 25,000 units at N4.00; Sales January: 13,000 units at N4.50; Sales February: 28,000 units at N5.00.
Using LIFO, determine the value of closing stock.
questions.explanation: Closing stock is 43,000 - 41,000 = 2,000 units; under LIFO these are the oldest units at N3.00, giving N6,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem:
Use the table: Opening balance 1/1/90: 3,000 units at N3.00; Purchases January: 15,000 units at N3.50; Purchases February: 25,000 units at N4.00; Sales January: 13,000 units at N4.50; Sales February: 28,000 units at N5.00.
What is the gross profit at the end of February, if the closing stock were valued at N20,000?

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: If a bad debt previously written off is subsequently repaid, the amount collected is recorded as an
options: income in the profit and loss account
addition cash in the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: A bad debt recovered is credited to profit and loss as income.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Beginning and ending accounts receivable balances were N8,000 and N15,000 respectively. If collections from customers during the period were N36,000, then total sales on account would be
questions.explanation: Credit sales = closing debtors + collections - opening debtors = 15,000 + 36,000 - 8,000 = N43,000.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: From which of the following sources is the creditors control account most likely to be posted?
questions.explanation: The credit purchases total in the purchases journal is posted to the creditors (purchases ledger) control account.

questions.stem: Which of the following categories of labour cost will be classified as direct?
questions.explanation: Wages of workers directly engaged in production are direct labour; the others are overheads.

questions.stem:
Use the information: Beginning inventory 20 units at N6 (N120); Sale No. 1: 18 units; Purchase No. 1: 30 units at N8 (N240); Sale No. 2: 20 units; Purchase No. 2: 10 units at N9 (N90). Totals: 60 units in, 38 units sold.
Using the FIFO method of stock valuation, the ending inventory cost is
questions.explanation: 22 units remain; under FIFO they are the latest: 10 x N9 + 12 x N8 = N186.

questions.stem:
Use the information: Beginning inventory 20 units at N6 (N120); Sale No. 1: 18 units; Purchase No. 1: 30 units at N8 (N240); Sale No. 2: 20 units; Purchase No. 2: 10 units at N9 (N90). Totals: 60 units in, 38 units sold.
Using the LIFO inventory procedures, the ending inventory cost is
questions.explanation: Under (periodic) LIFO the 22 remaining units are the earliest: 20 x N6 + 2 x N8 = N136.

questions.stem: The major difference between the receipt and payment account and the income and expenditure account is that while the former
options: is kept by the treasurer, the latter is not
deals with all receipts and payments in the year regardless of the time it relates to, the latter is for just that year
is a T-account, the latter is not
is not in the ledger, the latter is
questions.explanation: A receipts and payments account is a cash summary for all items received or paid, whereas the income and expenditure account includes only income and expenses of the year (accruals basis).

questions.stem: The following information relates to a hockey club: Subscription owing at the beginning N40; Subscription owing at the end N35; Subscription received in advance at the beginning N15; Subscription received during the period N2,560. The amount to be shown in the income and expenditure account would be
questions.explanation: Subscription income = 2,560 - 40 + 35 + 15 = N2,570.

questions.stem: The net profit from the trading account of a non-profit making organization would be treated as income in the
questions.explanation: Profit from a club's trading activity (e.g. a bar) is transferred to the income and expenditure account.

questions.stem:
Ada and Udo are lawyers who went into partnership as Ado & Co. Ada brought cash of N12,000, furnishing worth N18,000 and a motor vehicle worth N70,000. Udo on the other hand brought in cash N10,000, his building valued at N5,000 and a personal computer worth N135,000.
What is the capital of Ado & Co.?
questions.explanation: Ada contributes N100,000 and Udo N150,000, so total capital is N250,000.

questions.stem:
Ada and Udo are lawyers who went into partnership as Ado & Co. Ada brought cash of N12,000, furnishing worth N18,000 and a motor vehicle worth N70,000. Udo on the other hand brought in cash N10,000, his building valued at N5,000 and a personal computer worth N135,000.
What is the profit sharing ratio if it is based on capital contributed by Ada and Udo?
questions.explanation: Capitals are N100,000 (Ada) and N150,000 (Udo), a ratio of 2:3.

questions.stem: The major distinguishing element between the final accounts of a partnership and a sole trader is the
questions.explanation: A partnership prepares a profit and loss appropriation account to share profit among partners.

questions.stem: Goodwill appears in the books of a business only if it has been
options: raised in connection with the admission of a new partner
raised to account for the true value of a business on the death of a partner
raised in order to prevent the balance sheet showing that the business is insolvent
questions.explanation: Only purchased goodwill (paid for) is recorded as an asset in the books.

questions.stem: Under which of the following conditions is a partnership dissolved?
options: Change of the partnership's head office.
Purchase of a large quantity of fixed assets.
Retirement of a manager who is not a partner.
questions.explanation: A change in membership, such as admission of a new partner, dissolves the old partnership.

questions.stem: When shares issued are paid for, the accounting entry required is
options: debit bank or cash account and credit share capital and/or premium account
credit bank or cash account and debit share capital and/or premium account
debit shares account and credit capital account
credit shares account and debit capital account
questions.explanation: Cash received is debited to bank/cash and credited to share capital (and share premium where applicable).

questions.stem:
A limited liability company has an authorized share capital of N50 million split into 100 million shares. 80 million shares were offered for subscription at 60k per share payable in full on application. These have been fully subscribed and issued.
What is the nominal value of each share?
questions.explanation: Nominal value = N50 million / 100 million shares = N0.50.

questions.stem:
A limited liability company has an authorized share capital of N50 million split into 100 million shares. 80 million shares were offered for subscription at 60k per share payable in full on application. These have been fully subscribed and issued.
What is the issued capital?
questions.explanation: Issued capital at nominal value = 80 million x N0.50 = N40 million (the extra 10k per share is share premium).

questions.stem: The document setting out the regulations regarding shares, meetings and internal organization of a company is known as
questions.explanation: The articles of association govern the internal management of a company.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: An advantage of using accounting ratios is that they
questions.explanation: Ratios help users interpret financial statements and so aid decision-making.

questions.stem: The accounts of Buba (Nig.) Plc showed the following for the year ended December 31, 1993: Gross sales N219,900; Sales returns and allowances N4,900; Net sales N215,000; Accounts receivable (net): 1/1/93 N20,000, 31/12/93 N30,000. The turnover of accounts receivable is
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (20,000 + 30,000)/2 = 25,000; turnover = 215,000/25,000 = 8.6 times.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given: Sales N20,000; Cost of sales N15,000. The gross profit margin would be
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 5,000; margin = 5,000/20,000 = 25%.

questions.stem:
Perebeni Enterprises has two departments A and B, with the following information: Opening stock A N5,000, B N1,500; Purchases A N26,000, B N3,000; Closing stock A N7,000, B N2,500; Sales A N45,000, B N4,000. The following expenses are to be shared in the ratio 4:1: Rent N8,300; General expenses N3,200.
What is the company's gross profit for the year?

Perebeni Enterprises has two departments A and B, with the following information: Opening stock A N5,000, B N1,500; Purchases A N26,000, B N3,000; Closing stock A N7,000, B N2,500; Sales A N45,000, B N4,000. The following expenses are to be shared in the ratio 4:1: Rent N8,300; General expenses N3,200.
What is the net profit (or loss) contributed by department B?
questions.explanation: B's gross profit is N2,000 and its share of expenses is 1/5 of N11,500 = N2,300, giving a loss of N300.

questions.stem: The expenditure on a good or service which is consumed either immediately or within a current accounting period is called
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure covers items consumed within the current period.

questions.stem: The receipts from a special tax levy to pay maturing interest obligations are recorded in
questions.explanation: Resources set aside for paying interest and principal on debt are accounted for in a debt service fund.

questions.stem: The cash basis of accounting requires the recognition of revenues only when they are
questions.explanation: Under the cash basis revenue is recognised only when cash is received.

questions.stem: The amount for individual items on a government budget is called a
questions.explanation: Each appropriation head in a government budget is called a vote.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following factors has aided the development of accounting?
options: The discovery of mineral resources in commercial quantity
The growth in size of businesses and the separation of ownership and management
The development and management of a sophisticated monetary system
questions.explanation: As businesses grew and owners stopped managing them, owners needed accounts from managers (stewardship), driving the development of accounting.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following concepts stipulates that accounting profit is the difference between revenue and expenses?
questions.explanation: The accrual concept defines profit as revenue earned less expenses incurred, not cash received less cash paid.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: An effective accounting system should provide information
options: on internal and external reporting for managers and third parties
for promoters, directors, labour unions and distributors
questions.explanation: An accounting system serves both internal (management) and external (third-party) reporting needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following accounting records are source documents?
questions.explanation: Invoices and debit notes are source documents; journals, ledgers and cash books are books of account.

questions.stem: Given: Motor van N3,600; Premises N5,000; Loan from R. Nwaeke N1,000; Cash at bank N1,650; Stock of goods N4,800; Creditors N2,560; Cash in hand N250 and Debtors N6,910. Calculate the capital figure.
questions.explanation: Assets total N22,210 and liabilities N3,560, so capital = N18,650.

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions is BEST recorded in the general journal?
options: Payment of rent with a cheque.
Purchase of an asset on credit terms.
Transfer of cash from head office to branch.
questions.explanation: Credit purchases of fixed assets are not recorded in any special day book, so they go through the general journal.

questions.stem: Diamon Ringo business was started when Mr. Diamon brought in a cheque of N500,000 which was paid into the bank account. Which of the following entries properly records the transaction?
options: Cash account was credited with N500,000 and the capital account was debited with N500,000
Bank account was debited with N500,000 and capital account was credited with N500,000
Bank account was credited with N500,000 and capital account was debited with N500,000
Mr. Diamon's account was debited with N500,000 and the cheque account was credited with N500,000
questions.explanation: The bank receives the money (debit bank) and the owner's capital is credited.

questions.stem: A trial balance is usually prepared by an accountant from account balances in the ledger for the purpose of
options: testing arithmetical accuracy of the ledger account balances
providing a basis for establishing the accountant's competence
questions.explanation: The trial balance checks the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry in the ledger.

questions.stem: What are the advantages of an imprest petty cash book? (i) Cheque can be drawn easily (ii) A check on the use of cash (iii) Liability of the petty cashier is limited to the value of petty cash (iv) Losses through the petty cashier can be minimized.
questions.explanation: The imprest system controls the use of cash, limits the petty cashier's liability to the float and minimises losses.

questions.stem: Bola, UTC's regular customer, owed N1,000 on account of a radio bought. If he sent in a cheque for N1,500, UTC would send him a
questions.explanation: Bola overpaid by N500; his account now has a credit balance, which UTC acknowledges to him with a credit note.

questions.stem: A payment of cash of N20 to John was entered on the receipt side of the cashbook in error and credited to John's account. Which of the following journal entries can be used to correct the error?
options: John N40 Dr, Cash N40 Cr
Cash N40 Dr, John N40 Cr
John N20 Dr, Cash N20 Cr
Cash N20 Dr, John N20 Cr
questions.explanation: The correct entry was Dr John 20, Cr Cash 20; the reversed entry must be undone and redone, so Dr John N40, Cr Cash N40.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The following represents extracts from the trading account of a retail outlet for a given month: Opening stock N2,400; Closing stock N6,400; Other expenses N2,000; Sales N11,000; Profit N900. What is the purchase figure for the month?

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Why are adjustments in the profit and loss account necessary?
options: To cover some expenses of the following year.
To ascertain the actual expenses incurred and income earned during the year.
To show the provisions made during the year.
To show the total expenses paid and income received during the year.
questions.explanation: Adjustments (accruals, prepayments, provisions) ensure the account shows the expenses incurred and income earned for the year.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem:
MACHINERY: Historical cost N5,000,000.00; Estimated useful life 20 years; Residual value N25,000.00; Date of acquisition 1/1/71; Depreciation method: straight line.
Accumulated depreciation on the asset as at 31/12/81 was

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem:
MACHINERY: Historical cost N5,000,000.00; Estimated useful life 20 years; Residual value N25,000.00; Date of acquisition 1/1/71; Depreciation method: straight line.
The book value of the asset as at 31/12/86 was
questions.explanation: After 16 years accumulated depreciation is 16 x 248,750 = 3,980,000, so book value = N1,020,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem:
The following is a draft balance sheet as at 31/12/92: Fixed assets: cost N200,000, accumulated depreciation N100,000, net N100,000. Current assets: Stock in trade N10,000; Trade debtors N4,500; Cash at bank N22,800; Cash in hand N9,700. Trade creditors ?; Capital ?. Trade creditors' account was maintained at 25% of the capital.
What was the balance in the trade creditors account as at 31/12/92?
questions.explanation: Total assets = 147,000 = capital + 0.25 capital, so capital = 117,600 and creditors = N29,400.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem:
The following is a draft balance sheet as at 31/12/92: Fixed assets: cost N200,000, accumulated depreciation N100,000, net N100,000. Current assets: Stock in trade N10,000; Trade debtors N4,500; Cash at bank N22,800; Cash in hand N9,700. Trade creditors ?; Capital ?. Trade creditors' account was maintained at 25% of the capital.
What was the balance in the capital account as at 31/12/92?
questions.explanation: Total assets of N147,000 equal 1.25 x capital, so capital = N117,600.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The trial balance showed wages N2,500 and a note stated that N500 wages were due but unpaid. When preparing final accounts and balance sheet, it is required to debit profit and loss account with
options: N3,000 and show wages accrued N500 in the balance sheet
N2,000 and show wages accrued N500 in the balance sheet
N3,000 and show wages prepaid N500 in the balance sheet
N2,000 and show wages paid in advance N500 in the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Wages charged = 2,500 + 500 accrued = N3,000; the N500 owing is a current liability (accrual).

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Sales ledger control account contains the total amount in respect of
questions.explanation: The sales ledger control account summarises the debtors' accounts.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: The purchases ledger control account of a company had an opening balance of N45,600 credit and closing balance of N72,600 credit. The company made payments of N437,000 to credit suppliers during the period, and had discount received of N18,600 on this account. What were the credit purchases for the period?
The starting point for the production of accounts from incomplete records is to
options: compute the opening stock of goods sold
prepare an opening statement of affairs
questions.explanation: An opening statement of affairs establishes the opening capital, the starting point for incomplete records.

questions.stem:
I. A retailer when fixing his selling price adds one-quarter to the cost of the article. II. The expense of the retailer is 10% of his sales. III. The total sales is N23,000. IV. He turned over his stock five times in the year.
Compute the average amount of stock in hand at cost price.
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = 23,000/1.25 = 18,400; average stock = 18,400/5 = N3,680.

questions.stem:
I. A retailer when fixing his selling price adds one-quarter to the cost of the article. II. The expense of the retailer is 10% of his sales. III. The total sales is N23,000. IV. He turned over his stock five times in the year.
The net profit for the year is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 23,000 - 18,400 = 4,600; expenses = 10% of 23,000 = 2,300; net profit = N2,300.

questions.stem: The factory cost of goods produced is made up of
options: raw materials consumed and fixed cost
questions.explanation: Factory (production) cost = prime cost + factory overheads.

questions.stem: Subscriptions in arrears are
options: credited to the income and expenditure account and shown as a liability in the balance sheet
debited to the income and expenditure account and shown as an asset in the balance sheet
credited to the income and expenditure account and shown as an asset in the balance sheet
debited to the income and expenditure account and shown as a liability in the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Subscriptions due but unpaid are income of the year (credited to I&E) and an asset (amount owed by members).

questions.stem: Where a non-profit making organization prepares its accounts using the accruals basis of reporting, the statement showing how well the organization is doing is the
questions.explanation: The income and expenditure account, prepared on accruals, shows the surplus or deficit of the period.

questions.stem: A charitable club has the following figures: Subscriptions received in 1991 N2,800; Subscriptions unpaid in 1990 N300; Subscriptions paid for 1992 N150; Subscriptions due 1991 N180. How much should be charged to the income and expenditure of this club as subscription for 1991?

A member of a club paid N1,000 as his subscription for 1993 and N1,200 as subscription for 1994. If the financial year of the society ended on 31st December 1993, the N1,200 subscription will be treated in the balance sheet as
questions.explanation: Subscriptions received in advance are owed to members as a current liability.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strong feature of partnership?
options: The life of the partnership is generally assumed to be indefinite.
The owners are liable personally for all debts of the business.
The transfer of ownership is frequent and easy to accomplish.
The partnership is complex to form because of many legal and reporting requirements.
questions.explanation: Ordinary partners have unlimited liability for the firm's debts; the other statements describe companies, not partnerships.

questions.stem: Interest on a partner's drawings is debited to the
options: partner's current account and credited to the profit and loss appropriation account
profit and loss account and credited to the partner's current account
partner's current account and credited to the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Interest on drawings is charged to the partner (debit current account) and added to profit available (credit appropriation account).

questions.stem: A partnership on admitting a new member, revalued the business' land and building from N30,000 to N70,000. The difference of N40,000 should be
options: credited to land and building account
credited to profit and loss appropriation account
questions.explanation: A revaluation gain is debited to the asset and credited to the revaluation account.

questions.stem:
Halidu and Hamed are business partners with N30,000 and N20,000 capital respectively. At the end of the financial year, a profit of N12,000 which included Halidu's salary of N3,000 was made.
Halidu's share of the profit is
questions.explanation: After the N3,000 salary, N9,000 is shared in the capital ratio 3:2, so Halidu's share of profit is 3/5 x 9,000 = N5,400.

questions.stem:
Halidu and Hamed are business partners with N30,000 and N20,000 capital respectively. At the end of the financial year, a profit of N12,000 which included Halidu's salary of N3,000 was made.
Hamed's share of the profit should be
questions.explanation: With fixed capitals, a partner's share of profit is credited to his current account.

questions.stem: The conversion of a partnership business into a limited liability company affords the
options: general partners the chance of enjoying the limited liability protection
limited liability partners the chance of enjoying the limited liability protection
creditors the chance of enjoying the limited liability protection
debtors the chance of enjoying the limited liability protection
questions.explanation: General partners have unlimited liability; as shareholders of a limited company their liability becomes limited.

questions.stem:
Yakubu (Nigeria) Limited (Extract) Balance Sheet as at 31st December 1993: Ordinary shares: authorized N100,000, issued N80,000; 10% preference shares: authorized N30,000, issued N20,000; Share premium N20,000; Profit and loss A/C N13,000; Trade creditors N30,000; Accruals N5,000; Stock N10,000; Debtors N40,000; Bank N25,000.
Equity shareholders' fund is
questions.explanation: Equity = issued ordinary shares 80,000 + share premium 20,000 + profit and loss 13,000 = N113,000 (preference shares excluded).

questions.stem:
Yakubu (Nigeria) Limited (Extract) Balance Sheet as at 31st December 1993: Ordinary shares: authorized N100,000, issued N80,000; 10% preference shares: authorized N30,000, issued N20,000; Share premium N20,000; Profit and loss A/C N13,000; Trade creditors N30,000; Accruals N5,000; Stock N10,000; Debtors N40,000; Bank N25,000.
If a 10% dividend is approved, what is the dividend payable to ordinary shareholders?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 10% of issued ordinary capital of N80,000 = N8,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following ratios gives an idea of the liquidity of a firm?
questions.explanation: The quick (acid test) ratio measures liquidity.

questions.stem: A total of 400,000 shares of N1 each are to be issued by Sariki Company Ltd. at a price of N1.20 per share. Applications were received for 600,000 shares out of which 100,000 were dishonoured. If the available shares are distributed pro rata, what refund will be due a subscriber who applied for 5,000 shares?
questions.explanation: Valid applications 500,000 for 400,000 shares (4/5); he gets 4,000 shares costing N4,800, so of N6,000 paid N1,200 is refunded.

questions.stem: The measure of a company's ability to pay its debts quickly is called
questions.explanation: The acid test (quick) ratio measures the ability to meet debts quickly from liquid assets.

questions.stem: Departmental accounts are maintained to ascertain the
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts show the profit contribution of each department.

questions.stem: The Asa branch of Emene Company Ltd. made sales of N549,000 from the goods sent from the head office during the period ended 31/12/94. These sales were based on a 22% mark up. If branch expenses were N34,400 and there were no discrepancies, what should be the net profit of the branch for the period?
Which of the following statements is correct about the head office current account and the branch current account?
options: The head office current account has a credit balance while the branch current account has a debit balance.
The head office current account has a debit balance while the branch current account has a credit balance.
questions.explanation: The branch current account (in head office books) is a debit balance, while the head office current account (in the branch books) is a credit balance.

capital expenditure is equal to revenue
capital project fund is tied to recurrent expenditure

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The most important reason for studying accounting is that
options: the information provided by accounting is useful in making decisions
accounting plays an important role in a society
the study of accounting leads to a challenging career
questions.explanation: Accounting exists mainly to provide information that users rely on to make economic decisions.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting

questions.explanation: Creditors want to know whether the business can pay its debts as they fall due, i.e. its liquidity.

questions.stem: The instruments that are generated when firms enter into business transactions with others are called
questions.explanation: Invoices, receipts, credit notes etc. arising from transactions are collectively called source documents.

questions.stem: The document that is used to acknowledge the acceptance of the return of goods by the seller from the buyer is known as
questions.explanation: The seller issues a credit note to the buyer to acknowledge goods returned and reduce the amount owed.

questions.stem: The effect of the payment of a liability is that it
questions.explanation: Paying a creditor reduces cash (an asset) and reduces the amount owed (a liability).

questions.stem: Books of original entry are used for
options: reminding the bookkeeper to post transactions in the ledger
informing about the state of affairs
questions.explanation: Books of original (prime) entry are where transactions are first recorded before posting to the ledger.

questions.stem: The term posting in accounting refers to
options: transferring the balances in the ledger to the trial balance
tracing amounts from the journal to the ledger to find errors
transferring entries to the ledger from the journal
questions.explanation: Posting is the transfer of entries from the books of original entry (journal) to the ledger accounts.

questions.stem: Erroneous rearrangement of financial figures such as writing N624 as N264 is called
questions.explanation: Reversing the order of digits in a figure is an error of transposition.

options: Float -> expenses paid -> cash in bank -> float
Float -> cash from bank -> expenses paid -> float
Float -> expenses paid -> cash from bank -> float
Float -> cash in bank -> expenses paid -> float
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system the float is used to pay expenses, then exactly the amount spent is drawn from the bank to restore the float.

questions.explanation: A payment recorded in the cash book that the bank has not yet paid is a cheque issued but not yet presented: an unpresented cheque.

Uncredited cheques were: Bimpe N40; Wale N60, while unpresented cheques were: Usman N20, Kalu N32 and Musa N70. What is the cash book balance after the reconciliation?
questions.explanation: Bank balance 722 + uncredited cheques 100 - unpresented cheques 122 = N700.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: On 30/05/93 Tolu & Co. paid 2 years rent of N50,000 which was debited to the rent account. At 31/12/93, what portion of that amount was prepaid?
questions.explanation: Monthly rent = 50,000/24 = 2,083.33; June-December (7 months) has been used = 14,583, so 50,000 - 14,583 = N35,417 is prepaid.

questions.stem: The receipt of cash from a customer who bought goods with N800 list price, 25% trade discount and 2/10, n/30 terms would, if paid within the discount period, amount to
questions.explanation: Invoice value = 800 less 25% = 600; paying within 10 days earns 2% cash discount of 12, so cash received = N588.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: At the end of a financial period, the trading, profit and loss account of a company showed a profit of N120,000. It was however recorded that revenue of N12,000 was recorded as expenses while expenses of N4,000 had been recorded as revenue. What should be the correct profit for the period?
questions.explanation: Correcting the N12,000 revenue shown as expense adds 24,000; correcting the N4,000 expense shown as revenue deducts 8,000: 120,000 + 24,000 - 8,000 = N136,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given capital, N13,000; office machinery, N9,000; creditors, N900; stock of goods, N1,550; debtors, N275; cash at bank, N5,075 and loan from Jumbo, N2,000. What is the balance sheet total?
questions.explanation: Assets 9,000 + 1,550 + 275 + 5,075 = 15,900, which equals capital 13,000 + creditors 900 + loan 2,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The recording of wages due but not yet paid is an example of an adjustment for

questions.explanation: Wages incurred but unpaid at the year end are accrued expenses.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The process of allocating the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life is known as
questions.explanation: Writing off the cost of intangible assets (e.g. goodwill, patents) over their useful lives is amortization.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: The principal use of control accounts is to
questions.explanation: Control accounts check the arithmetical accuracy of each ledger, so errors can be localized to a particular ledger.

questions.stem: In the absence of a sales day book or sales account, the credit for sales can be computed from
options: opening figures of the balance sheet
closing figures of the balance sheet
questions.explanation: Credit sales are the balancing figure in a total debtors (debtors control) account.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Which of the following conditions best represents the net effect of discount allowed on credit sales on the account of a business?
options: Decrease in the closing balance of sales ledger control account
Increase in the values of sales
Decrease in the value of purchases in the trading account
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is credited to the debtors (sales ledger control) account, reducing the amount debtors owe; it is also an expense, so it does not raise profit.

questions.stem: The total of the creditors at the beginning of the year was N4,600 and at the end of the year N5,250. During the year, N26,500 was paid to suppliers and N130 was received in discounts from these suppliers. The purchases for the year would be
questions.explanation: Purchases = payments 26,500 + discounts 130 + closing creditors 5,250 - opening creditors 4,600 = N27,280.

questions.stem: Given: Capital at the beginning N20,000; Drawings N3,000; Capital at end N30,000; New capital introduced N8,000. What is the profit for the period?
questions.explanation: Profit = closing capital - opening capital + drawings - new capital = 30,000 - 20,000 + 3,000 - 8,000 = N5,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following stock valuation methods is suitable under inflationary conditions?
questions.explanation: LIFO charges the most recent (higher) prices to cost of sales, so it matches current costs with revenue when prices are rising.

questions.stem: Given: Direct material N10,000; Direct labour N5,000; Direct expenses N2,000; Factory overhead N4,000. What is the prime cost?
questions.explanation: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses = 10,000 + 5,000 + 2,000 = N17,000.

questions.stem: The understatement of closing value of work-in-process would have the effect of
options: overstating prime cost of goods manufactured
understating prime cost of goods manufactured
questions.explanation: Closing work-in-progress is deducted in the manufacturing account, so understating it overstates the cost of goods manufactured; prime cost is unaffected.

questions.stem: The difference between a trading account and a manufacturing account is that while the manufacturing account
options: has no particular period, the trading account has
does not consider the cost of goods involved, the trading account does
is concerned with the cost of production, the trading account is not
is not concerned with the stock of raw materials, the trading account is
questions.explanation: The manufacturing account computes the cost of production; the trading account compares sales with the cost of goods sold.

questions.stem: An income and expenditure account is a summary of
options: all income and expenditure during a period
revenue income and expenditure during a period
receipts and payments during a period
the trading income during a period
questions.explanation: The income and expenditure account records only revenue (not capital) income and expenditure of the period, on an accruals basis.

questions.stem: Gbagada Social Club - Receipts and Payments Account for the year 1993: Receipts - Balance b/d N720; Subscriptions N14,300; Proceeds from raffle draws N2,000 (total N17,020). Payments - Rent N180; Furniture N3,500; Rate N580; Stationery N120; Welfare expenses N1,000; Raffle prize N950; Balance c/d N10,690 (total N17,020). Additional information (1/1/93 and 31/12/93 respectively): Subscription in arrears N300, N450; Furniture N7,000 (1/1/93); Subscription received in advance N500, N400; Rate owing N50, N60. Subscription relating to the accounting year 1993 in the income and expenditure account is
questions.explanation: Subscriptions = 14,300 - opening arrears 300 + closing arrears 450 + opening advance 500 - closing advance 400 = N14,550.

questions.stem: Adamu, Babaji and Chukwu are in partnership and they share profits and losses in the ratio 3:2:1. Their respective capitals are N20,000, N15,000 and N5,000 on which they are entitled to interest at 5% per annum. The profit for the year before charging interest on capital amounted to N5,500. Calculate the profit for Adamu.
questions.explanation: Interest on capital = 1,000 + 750 + 250 = 2,000; residual profit 3,500 shared 3:2:1 gives Adamu 3/6 x 3,500 = N1,750.

questions.stem: Faruk and Osawe are in partnership sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:7. Faruk is to receive a salary of N9,000. In one accounting period, the business recorded a loss of N1,500 (before deduction of Faruk's salary). The appropriate distribution of the net loss would be
questions.explanation: After Faruk's salary the loss is 1,500 + 9,000 = 10,500, shared 3:7: Faruk 3,150 and Osawe 7,350.

questions.stem: On partnership dissolution, if a partner's capital account has a debit balance and the partner is insolvent, the deficiency will, in accordance with the decision in the case of Garner v Murray, be
questions.explanation: Garner v Murray: the deficiency of an insolvent partner is borne by the solvent partners in the ratio of their last agreed capitals.

questions.stem: Share premium can be used to: i. write off discount on shares; ii. give loans to directors; iii. pay dividends; iv. pay company's formation expenses
questions.explanation: Share premium may be used to write off discounts on shares and preliminary (formation) expenses, or for bonus issues; it cannot be paid out as dividends or lent to directors.

questions.stem: A company has 5% debentures worth N500,000, ordinary capital N2,000,000, and preference shares N1,500,000. If the company made a profit of N1,000,000, the debenture interest would amount to
questions.explanation: Debenture interest is a fixed charge on the debenture value: 5% x 500,000 = N25,000, regardless of profit.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Udoh Trading Company - Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 1992: Capital N39,000; Term loan N15,000; Creditors N9,000; Accrued wages N5,000 (total N68,000). Land N20,000; Building N30,000; Stock N4,000; Cash N8,000; Debtors N6,000 (total N68,000). What is the working capital?
questions.explanation: Current assets 4,000 + 8,000 + 6,000 = 18,000 less current liabilities 9,000 + 5,000 = 14,000 gives N4,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Udoh Trading Company - Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 1992: Capital N39,000; Term loan N15,000; Creditors N9,000; Accrued wages N5,000 (total N68,000). Land N20,000; Building N30,000; Stock N4,000; Cash N8,000; Debtors N6,000 (total N68,000). The acid test ratio in the company is
questions.explanation: Acid test = (current assets - stock) / current liabilities = (18,000 - 4,000) / 14,000 = 1:1.

questions.stem: Which of the following are advantages of departmental accounts? (i) The department making the highest profit can be easily determined (ii) The capital of the business can be calculated easily (iii) Easy knowledge of the sources of funding (iv) Encouragement of healthy rivalry among the various departments.
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts show the result of each department, identifying the most profitable and encouraging healthy competition between departments.

questions.stem: The end result of governmental accounting procedure is to
options: keep proper records of government expenditures
give financial information to the public and investors
produce timely and accurate financial reports for legislators and the public
give information on the performance of public enterprises
questions.explanation: Government accounting culminates in timely, accurate financial reports that account to the legislature and the public for public funds.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The Act establishing the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) came into force on
questions.explanation: ICAN was established by Act No. 15 of 1965, which came into force on 1st September 1965.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Cost reports for the attention of management should reflect
options: cost and comparable data useful in decision-making
questions.explanation: Management reports should give relevant cost and comparative data that help managers make decisions.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Responsibility accounting is particularly concerned with
questions.explanation: Responsibility accounting holds each manager accountable for the costs he can control.

questions.stem: An advantage of the use of the voucher system is that it
options: reduces the number of cheques that will be written during any given period
provides a highly flexible system for handling unusual transactions
provides a comprehensive record of business done with particular suppliers
ensures that every expenditure is reviewed and verified before payment is made
questions.explanation: Under a voucher system each payment must be supported by an approved voucher, so every expenditure is checked before it is paid.

questions.stem: A business transaction is recorded in the books of accounts when the
options: owner of the business invests his N10,000 in another company
business retains part of its profits for future expansion purposes
business applies for overdraft facilities from its bankers
owner of the business collects N5,000 from the accountant
questions.explanation: Only the owner taking N5,000 out of the business (drawings) changes the business's assets and capital; the others are private or non-monetary events.

questions.stem: When a transaction causes an asset account to increase, there is
options: a decrease of equal amount in the owner's equity account
an increase in a liability account
an increase of equal amount in another asset account
a decrease of equal amount in a liability account
questions.explanation: By the accounting equation an increase in an asset must be matched by an increase in a liability or capital, or a decrease in another asset; of the options only an increase in a liability fits.

questions.stem: The purchase of two generators by Hassan Electronics Enterprises should be recorded as
options: an expense in its general office expenses column
a part of capital in the capital account
questions.explanation: Generators bought for use (not resale) in the business are fixed assets.

questions.stem: The total of the discounts received column in the cash book is posted to the
options: credit of the discounts received account
debit of the discounts allowed account
credit of the discounts allowed account
debit of the discounts received account
questions.explanation: Discount received is a gain, so the cash book column total is credited to the discounts received account.

questions.stem: The initial imprest as at July 1st was N500. Petty cash vouchers with the custodian by July 15th added up to N394. An IOU slip received from a co-worker was N65 and there was a shortage of N5 cash. The co-worker made refund on July 18th just before the imprest was replenished. What was the actual cash in the till as at 15th July?
questions.explanation: Cash in till = 500 - vouchers 394 - IOU 65 - shortage 5 = N36.

questions.stem: The initial imprest as at July 1st was N500. Petty cash vouchers with the custodian by July 15th added up to N394. An IOU slip received from a co-worker was N65 and there was a shortage of N5 cash. The co-worker made refund on July 18th just before the imprest was replenished. The amount required to replenish the payments made from the imprest was
questions.explanation: After the IOU refund cash is 36 + 65 = 101, so 500 - 101 = N399 (vouchers 394 plus the shortage 5) restores the imprest.

questions.stem: State Bank collected a note for Al-Makura Company. This collection, not yet recorded in Al-Makura's books, appears on the bank reconciliation as
options: an addition to balance per books
a deduction from balance per bank statement
an addition to balance per bank statement
a deduction from balance per books
questions.explanation: The bank has already credited the collection; the company must add it to its cash book (balance per books).

questions.stem: Mayana Corporation uses special journals to record its transactions. If one of Mayana's customers returns merchandise purchased with cash (for a refund), it makes an entry in the
questions.explanation: A cash refund to a customer is a cash payment, recorded in the cash disbursements (payments) journal.

questions.stem: Sobande Incorporation acquired a machine that involved the following expenditures and related factors: Gross invoice price N15,000; Sales tax N900; Purchases discount taken N300; Freight N750; Assembly of machine N500; Installation of machine N800; Assorted spare parts for future use N1,200; Turning and adjusting machine N700. What is the initial accounting cost of the machine?
questions.explanation: Cost = 15,000 + 900 - 300 + 750 + 500 + 800 + 700 = N18,350; spare parts for future use are not part of the machine cost.
