What is the balance on its cash account as at 31/1/95?

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: On 1st January, 1993, Lobo Company purchased equipment for N18,000. It uses straight-line depreciation and estimates an eight-year useful life and a N2,000 salvage value. On 31st December, 1996, it sells the equipment for N8,000. In recording this sale, it should reflect
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (18,000 - 2,000)/8 = 2,000; after 4 years book value = 10,000; selling for 8,000 gives a N2,000 loss.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: The balance on a purchases ledger control account represents the
options: present amount that a business owes its suppliers at date
total credit available to the business at the end of the year to be utilized in future
total credit the business enjoyed for the particular year from its suppliers
total credit owed the business by its customers
questions.explanation: The purchases ledger control account balance is the total owed to trade creditors at that date.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: A powerful instrument of control over both the sales ledger and the clerk whose duty is to post the ledger is the
questions.explanation: The total debtors (sales ledger control) account checks the accuracy of the sales ledger and of the clerk posting it.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Mini Enterprises sales ledger as at 31/12/94 read: Balance b/f N12,750; Total credit sales N28,185; Payments by debtors N12,112; Discount allowed N638; Sales returns N1,500. Prepare the sales ledger control account and determine the balance due from debtors.
Determine the year's purchases from the following information relating to a firm: Total creditors b/f N7,200; Total cash payments to suppliers N98,800; Total creditors c/f N8,400.
questions.explanation: Purchases = payments 98,800 + closing creditors 8,400 - opening creditors 7,200 = N100,000.

questions.stem: Derive the total sales figure from the following information extracted from a firm's cash book and other relevant records: Total debtors b/f N5,600; Total cash receipts from debtors and cash sales N153,000; Total debtors c/f N6,800.
questions.explanation: Total sales = receipts 153,000 + closing debtors 6,800 - opening debtors 5,600 = N154,200.

questions.stem: The statement of affairs prepared from incomplete records can be described as
options: the summary of all the business transactions of the trader ascertained by the accountant
a balance sheet at a particular date showing the assets and liabilities of the business
a schedule of all the business ventures entered into for the period to which the records relate
the statement that shows the profit or loss made during the period
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs lists assets and liabilities at a date to find capital; it is effectively a balance sheet.

questions.stem: The contribution margin on a job is the
options: excess of sales revenue over variable costs
difference between fixed and variable costs
questions.explanation: Contribution = sales revenue - variable costs.

questions.stem: The objective of allocating all costs to products is to
options: avoid unallocated overhead and compute total product cost
co-ordinate the cost and financial accounts
compute the contribution of the product to the final profit
questions.explanation: Absorbing all costs into products ensures no overhead is left unallocated and gives the full (total) product cost.

questions.stem: Raw materials inventory at the beginning of a period was N46,800 and at the close of the period there was a balance of N38,600. From the purchases made during the period, defective materials costing N9,200 were returned. Cost of materials consumed during the period was N448,500. What was the total purchases made during the period?
questions.explanation: Net purchases = 448,500 + 38,600 - 46,800 = 440,300; adding back returns of 9,200 gives total purchases of N449,500.

questions.stem: Raw materials inventory at the beginning of a period was N46,800 and at the close of the period there was a balance of N38,600. From the purchases made during the period, defective materials costing N9,200 were returned. Cost of materials consumed during the period was N448,500. What is the cost of materials available for use during the period?
questions.explanation: Materials available = opening stock 46,800 + net purchases 440,300 = N487,100 (= consumed 448,500 + closing 38,600).

questions.stem: A non-profit-making organization differs from a profit-making one in that
options: proceeds from sale of shares form part of its income
annual subscriptions and levies form part of its income
questions.explanation: A club's income comes mainly from members' subscriptions and levies rather than trading profit.

questions.stem: The limitations of the receipts and payments account arise mainly because of the reliance on
options: cash movement as evidence of transaction
the capital account of the organization
the transaction papers as evidence of transaction
questions.explanation: A receipts and payments account records only cash movements, ignoring accruals, prepayments and non-cash items.

questions.stem: The trading account is to a sole trader what income and expenditure account is to a
questions.explanation: Non-profit-making organizations prepare an income and expenditure account in place of a trading and profit and loss account.

questions.stem: Which of the following indicate that a partnership business is in place? (i) there is a business (ii) it is run commonly by partners (iii) it has profit-making in view (iv) partners' liability is limited.
questions.explanation: A partnership is the relation between persons carrying on a business in common with a view of profit; liability of ordinary partners is unlimited.

questions.stem: When forming a partnership, new partners should record non-monetary assets on the new partnership's books at
options: their historical costs when first used
their historical costs when first purchased by each new partner
the highest values practical so that future income tax deductions are maximized
questions.explanation: Assets contributed to a new partnership are recorded at their agreed current fair values so each partner is credited fairly.

questions.stem: Umar and Ahmed share profits and losses equally and have capital balances of N40,000 and N60,000 respectively. If Abdullahi purchases a one-third interest with no bonus, how much will he have to contribute to the partnership?
questions.explanation: With no bonus his capital X must be one-third of (100,000 + X), so X = 50,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an intangible asset and a measure of a firm's superior earning power?
questions.explanation: Goodwill represents the ability of a business to earn profits above the normal return on its net assets.

questions.stem: Dan & Baker are in partnership with capitals of N50,000 and N30,000 each. The partnership agreement provides that: (i) profits be shared in the ratio of capital (ii) Baker be paid a salary of N8,000 (iii) both partners pay interest on drawings at 6% p.a. At the end of the year, Dan drew N15,000 while Baker drew N14,000 in four equal instalments on 31/3, 30/6, 30/9 and 31/12. The net profit for the year was N48,000. N5,000 is to be written off the Goodwill account. What is the interest on the drawings by Baker?
questions.explanation: Each instalment is 3,500; interest at 6% for 9, 6, 3 and 0 months = 3,500 x 6% x 18/12 = N315.

questions.stem: The ordinary shareholders enjoy the following rights except the right to
options: participate in additional issues of shares
receive dividends at a predetermined rate
questions.explanation: A fixed (predetermined) dividend rate belongs to preference shares, not ordinary shares.

questions.stem: Granada Corporation has net assets of N600,000 and contributed capital of N180,000. The corporation has 30,000 shares of common stock outstanding with no preferred stock. This suggests that the corporation has
options: a book value of N14 per share
a book value of N20 per share
questions.explanation: Book value per share = net assets 600,000 / 30,000 shares = N20 (retained earnings would be 420,000, not a deficit).

questions.stem: Under which of these conditions can a company issue shares at discount? (i) a resolution must be passed at a general meeting (ii) the amount of discount must be stated in the resolution (iii) the share must have existed for at least six years (iv) on the order of a court.
questions.explanation: Issue at a discount requires a general-meeting resolution specifying the discount and sanction of the court; there is no six-year requirement.

questions.stem: The part of equity which is payable on winding up is called
questions.explanation: Capital reserves cannot be distributed as dividends; they are returned to shareholders only on winding up.

questions.stem: To compute gearing ratio, divide
questions.explanation: Gearing measures the proportion of fixed-interest long-term debt to equity capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following entries is effected by a department when goods are charged to it at selling prices?
questions.explanation: Goods charged to a department at selling price are debited to the department's stock account, with the mark-up credited to a mark-up (adjustment) account.

questions.stem: The difference between the closure of the books of a branch and those of a separate company is that
options: there is retained earnings account on the branch books
the revenue and expense account is closed to branch current account
there is no retained earnings account on the branch books
the revenue and expense account is not closed to the home office current account
questions.explanation: A branch closes its profit to the head office current account and keeps no retained earnings account of its own.

questions.stem: The term fiscal compliance means
options: all financial and related laws and regulations are adhered to
only the budget for the current period is complied with and no deficits allowed
all physical assets requirements have been met
fiscal planning is necessary for proper accountability in the public sector
questions.explanation: Fiscal compliance means observing all financial laws, regulations and rules governing public funds.

questions.stem: In a public corporation, the capital expenditure incurred in a financial period is
options: spread over the useful life of the assets through depreciation
apportioned at a pre-determined rate stipulated by law
written off in the year in which they occur
merged with recurrent expenditure and reported in one lump sum
questions.explanation: Public corporations keep commercial (accrual) accounts, so capital expenditure is capitalised and depreciated over the asset life.

questions.stem: Money not required to meet chargeable expenditure in any fiscal year under cash accounting should be
options: surrendered to the consolidated revenue fund
carried forward to the next financial year
reserved to meet any deficits or contingencies
questions.explanation: Under cash accounting unspent appropriations lapse at year end and are surrendered to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

questions.stem: If a monthly insurance premium is remitted to a company by the state government, the initial deductions from employees are recorded in
questions.explanation: Amounts withheld from employees and held for remittance to third parties are accounted for in an agency fund.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The basic role of accounting is to
questions.explanation: Accounting exists to measure and report the performance and position of an entity; fraud detection and attestation are audit functions.

questions.stem: When a proprietor withdraws cash from the business for private use, he
options: debits cash account and credits drawings account
credits cash account and debits bank account
debits bank account and credits drawings account
credits cash account and debits drawings account
questions.explanation: Cash leaves the business (credit cash) and the owner's drawings increase (debit drawings).

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: A basic unifying concept in accounting implies that
options: where creditors' account is zero, the assets are equal to the owner's equity
there should be a balance in the creditors' account in order to measure total assets
revenues should be supported by invested and owner's capital
total assets can be less than liability and equity
questions.explanation: The accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Owner's equity means that with zero liabilities, assets equal owner's equity.

questions.stem: A source document for the sales day book is
questions.explanation: Credit sales are entered in the sales day book from copies of sales invoices.

questions.stem: In a cash book, the opening balance was N7,600, closing balance N9,200 and the total cash received during the period was N18,000. What was the amount of cash paid out during the period?
questions.explanation: Payments = opening balance + receipts − closing balance = 7,600 + 18,000 − 9,200 = N16,400.

questions.stem: If the total discount allowed in the cash book was N230 and the total discount received was N255, which of the following is true concerning the two discounts?
options: They must be balanced in the cash book and the difference taken to the debtors ledger
They must be balanced in the cash book and the difference taken to the trial balance
They should not be balanced in the cash book before being taken to the trial balance
They should not appear in the trial balance as they were already either received or paid out
questions.explanation: The discount columns are memorandum columns: they are simply totalled (not balanced) and each total is posted to the discount allowed and discount received accounts, which then appear in the trial balance.

questions.stem: Which of the following bank reconciliation items should not be added to or subtracted from the bank statement balance to determine the adjusted cash balance?
options: Deposits in the mail not yet received by the bank
Bank error, charging a company for another company's cheques
questions.explanation: Bank service charges are already in the bank statement; they are adjusted in the cash book, not against the bank statement balance.

questions.stem: The fixed amount of money given to a petty cashier at the beginning of a period is called
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system the petty cashier starts each period with a fixed sum called the imprest.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: A provision for bad debt account had N3,800 at the beginning of the year and N4,220 at the close of the year. If bad debts are calculated at the rate of 1/20% of annual credit sales, what was the credit sales for the period?

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: A company bought a vehicle worth N20,000 and the vehicle is to be depreciated at 5% using the reducing balance method of depreciation. What would be the value of the asset after 3 years?

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Use the information below: Capital: opening balance N307,000; closing balance N342,000. Net profit for the period N121,600. Opening stock N98,800. Purchases N706,000. Carriage inwards N17,500. Cost of goods sold N740,700. Total selling, general and administrative expenses N526,000. Discount received N9,650. What is the closing stock for the period?
questions.explanation: Closing stock = opening stock + purchases + carriage inwards − cost of goods sold = 98,800 + 706,000 + 17,500 − 740,700 = N81,600.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Use the information below: Capital: opening balance N307,000; closing balance N342,000. Net profit for the period N121,600. Opening stock N98,800. Purchases N706,000. Carriage inwards N17,500. Cost of goods sold N740,700. Total selling, general and administrative expenses N526,000. Discount received N9,650. Calculate the gross profit for the period.
questions.explanation: Net profit = gross profit + discount received − expenses, so gross profit = 121,600 + 526,000 − 9,650 = N637,950.

questions.stem: Chibuike bought 36 notebooks at N10 each from John and was given a trade discount of 5%. In addition, he was offered 1% cash discount which he took advantage of. How much did Chibuike pay?
questions.explanation: 360 less 5% trade discount = 342; less 1% cash discount = 342 × 0.99 = N338.58.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Depreciation on a particular piece of machinery was N2,700 during the fifth year of its service life and N4,050 during the sixth year. The logical explanation for this is that
options: an addition was made to the asset during the sixth year
the estimate of salvage value on this equipment was decreased at the beginning of the fifth year
a unit-of-output method of depreciation was used during the sixth year
the estimated remaining service life of the asset was increased at the beginning of the sixth year
questions.explanation: A rise in the depreciation charge in year six only is explained by an addition to the asset's cost that year; a longer life would reduce the charge and a salvage change in year five would affect year five too.

questions.stem: The main features of the single entry system are that
options: books of accounts are not maintained and business relies only on bank statement
the journal records are absent and only the main ledger is kept
there are incomplete classifications and recording procedures
only credit sales transactions and credit purchases are recorded
questions.explanation: Single entry is not a full double-entry system: records (usually a cash book and personal accounts) are incomplete in classification and recording.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: The principal function of a sales ledger control account is to
options: serve as internal check and provide quick information for the preparation of interim financial statements
serve as external check and provide quick information for the preparation of interim financial statements
provide quick information for the preparation of customers' statements
provide information for the control of salesmen's activities
questions.explanation: Control accounts act as an internal check on the sales ledger and quickly give total debtors for interim accounts.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Use the information below: Aminu and Sons credit purchases (Extract) as at February, 1996: Feb 1 credit balances N40,000; debit balances N1,000. Feb 28 purchases journal totals N500,000; returns outwards journal total N50,000; cheques paid to suppliers N400,000; promissory notes sent to suppliers N30,000; discount received from suppliers N8,000; credit balances in the purchases ledger set off against debit balances in the sales ledger N2,000. The total for the purchases ledger control account is
questions.explanation: The credit side holds the opening credit balances 40,000 + purchases 500,000 = N540,000, which is the total of each side once the balance is carried down.

questions.stem: Given: Total cash received from debtors N30,000; total purchases for the period N21,000; amount owed by debtors at the beginning of the period N4,000; equipment bought N2,500; amount owed by debtors at the end of the period N3,000. Determine the value of sales for the period.
questions.explanation: Sales = cash received + closing debtors − opening debtors = 30,000 + 3,000 − 4,000 = N29,000.

questions.stem: When the factory cost of production has been ascertained, manufactured goods are transferred to trading accounts by
options: debiting manufacturing account and crediting trading account
crediting sales account and debiting trading account
debiting sales account and crediting trading account
crediting manufacturing account and debiting trading account
questions.explanation: The cost of goods manufactured is credited to the manufacturing account and debited to the trading account.

questions.stem: Lawal and Co makes blocks and sells to builders. In computing prime cost, which of the following costs would be considered appropriate?
options: Sales boys' wages, cement and sand
Carriage outwards, carriage inwards and cement
questions.explanation: Prime cost is direct materials (cement, water, carriage inwards on materials) plus direct labour; carriage outwards and sales wages are selling costs.

questions.stem: Manufacturing cost can be classified based on
options: timing of charges, degree of averaging, ease of traceability and timing of charges
degree of averaging and size of capital
number of employed, timing of charges and management style
questions.explanation: Manufacturing costs are classified by timing of charge (product/period), degree of averaging and traceability (direct/indirect).

questions.stem: The difference between the factory cost of production and prime cost of production is
questions.explanation: Factory cost of production = prime cost + factory overheads.

questions.stem: Receipts and payments account of a non-profit making organisation is principally a summary of the
questions.explanation: A receipts and payments account summarises the cash book for the period.

questions.stem: Given: Club debtors at start N150; cash sales N4,850; club debtors at close N900; cash received from debtors N550. What is the amount of club sales?
A credit balance on a receipts and payments account indicates that the non-profit making organisation
options: had more revenues than expenses during the period
did not owe much liabilities during the period
received more cash than it paid out during the period
made more cash payments than it received during the period
questions.explanation: The account is a cash summary, so a credit balance (overdraft) means payments exceeded the cash available from receipts.

questions.stem: Goodwill can be valued in partnership when
questions.explanation: Goodwill is valued on changes in the partnership such as retirement, admission or death of a partner.

questions.stem: As part of the initial investment, a partner contributes office equipment that originally cost N20,000 and on which provision for depreciation of N12,500 had been recorded. If the partners agree on a valuation of N9,000 for the equipment, what amount should be debited to the office equipment account?
questions.explanation: Assets contributed by a partner are recorded at the agreed (fair) value, N9,000.

questions.stem: When a partner makes a drawing of stock items from a partnership, the accounting impact of the drawing is to increase the partner's
options: profit and loss account credit balance
questions.explanation: Drawings (cash or goods) are debited to the partner's current account, increasing its debit balance.

questions.stem: Appropriation account: Interest on capital: Kudu N750, Wale N550; Salaries: Kudu N800, Wale N600; Share of profits: Kudu N3,300, Wale N3,300. Determine the net profit of the partnership.
questions.explanation: Net profit = all appropriations = 750 + 550 + 800 + 600 + 3,300 + 3,300 = N9,300.

questions.stem: Dele and Seun, who are in partnership, have decided to convert their business into a limited liability company where both become directors. To convert the business
options: they will simply continue since there are no new members
the partnership is formally ended and new company books opened
the shares and all other items will be shared equally and not in their former ratios
computation of goodwill must be done as it is legally required
questions.explanation: On conversion the partnership is dissolved (realisation account) and a new set of books is opened for the company.

questions.stem: If a sole proprietorship is purchased for cash, then
options: the purchaser debits his business purchase account with the consideration he pays
all assets and liabilities must be bought
goodwill results where the value of liabilities taken is higher than the value of assets
the vendor debits his business purchase account with the consideration he receives
questions.explanation: The purchaser debits business purchase account with the purchase consideration and credits the vendor (then cash).

questions.stem: The market price per ordinary share of a corporation listed on the stock exchange is most closely related to its
questions.explanation: Share prices reflect expected earnings, so they move most closely with earnings per share.

questions.stem: Which of the following events increases a corporation's shareholders' equity?
options: Donation of shares out of the corporation's own stock to the corporation
The corporation's purchase of treasury stock
Shares of previously subscribed stock issued to subscribing stockholders
A municipality's donation of land to the corporation
questions.explanation: A donation of land adds an asset with no liability, increasing equity (donated capital); buying treasury stock reduces equity and the others leave it unchanged.

questions.stem: Zoom Plc Balance Sheet (Extract) as at 31st December 1997 shows: paid-up capital N200,000; share premium N15,000; profit & loss account N60,000. Determine the owner's equity.
questions.explanation: Owner's equity = paid-up capital + share premium + profit and loss balance = 200,000 + 15,000 + 60,000 = N275,000.

questions.stem: If a promoter pays a lawyer N5,000 for services rendered in preparing a Memorandum of Incorporation, the journal entry is to debit
questions.explanation: Costs of forming a company are preliminary expenses: debit preliminary expenses, credit cash.

questions.stem: Calls in advance are treated in the balance sheet as
questions.explanation: Calls in advance are money received before it is due and owed back to shareholders until the call is made, so they are shown as a liability (current).

questions.stem: Shares issued to a vendor in payment of business purchased would require a debit to
options: cash account and credit to share capital account
share capital account and credit to vendor's account
vendor's account and credit to share capital account
share capital account and credit to cash account
questions.explanation: Issuing shares discharges the amount owed to the vendor: debit vendor, credit share capital.

questions.stem: To record the transfer of stock from one department to another, the correct entry would be to debit
options: goods outwards and credit goods inwards
merchandise account and credit department stock account
department transferring and credit department receiving
department receiving and credit department transferring
questions.explanation: The receiving department gains stock (debit) and the transferring department loses it (credit).

questions.stem: Amoga Limited invoiced goods at a cost of N10,000 to its Ikeja branch at a margin of 20%. The branch later returned goods worth N1,200 at invoice price to the head office. The profit margin should be
options: debited to goods sent to branch account
debited to branch stock adjustment account
questions.explanation: The loading (unrealised profit) on goods sent to the branch is credited to the branch stock adjustment account.

questions.stem: Which of the following accounts is kept by local governments in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Local governments keep cash-based government accounts such as advances accounts; they do not prepare profit and loss accounts.

questions.stem: The conventional sources of public revenue include
options: loans, taxation, foreign reserves and dividends
crude oil, interest, posted price and taxation
taxation, deficit budgeting, royalties and loans
questions.explanation: Interest, royalties, taxation and loans are conventional sources; foreign reserves, posted price and deficit budgeting are not revenue sources.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: On November 1, 1998, Zaria Holdings owed N13,600 in respect of a creditor. On November 15, it purchased goods worth N69,000 and paid a cheque of N51,600. On November 29, one of the Holdings' cheques worth N3,000 was returned while the creditor granted N1,500 discount. The amount owed by Zaria Holdings as at November 29 is
questions.explanation: 13,600 + 69,000 − 51,600 + 3,000 (dishonoured cheque restores the debt) − 1,500 discount = N32,500.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: To write off bad debt, debit
options: debtor's account and credit provision for bad debt
bad debt account and credit debtor's account
debtor's account and credit bad debt
questions.explanation: Writing off a bad debt: debit bad debts account, credit the debtor's account.

questions.stem: In order to make the cash book balance equal to the bank statement, it is usual to add
questions.explanation: Starting from the cash book balance, unpresented cheques are added back because the bank has not yet paid them.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Use the information: Sales N20,000; cost of sales N10,000; operating expenses N2,500; expenses prepaid included in operating expenses N500. Calculate the net profit.
questions.explanation: Operating expenses for the period = 2,500 − 500 prepaid = 2,000; net profit = 20,000 − 10,000 − 2,000 = N8,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Use the information: Sales N20,000; cost of sales N10,000; operating expenses N2,500; expenses prepaid included in operating expenses N500. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.explanation: Gross profit 10,000 ÷ sales 20,000 = 50%.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The main object of book keeping is to record economic
options: transactions systematically for routine managerial decision making
events clearly to ensure adequate checks and balances
events clearly to facilitate strategic managerial decision-making
transactions systematically to ascertain the financial position of a business
questions.explanation: Book keeping records transactions systematically so that the results and financial position of the business can be ascertained.

questions.stem: A source document that aids the ascertainment of amount paid out of a current account is the
questions.explanation: The cheque stub (counterfoil) retained by the drawer records amounts paid out of the current account.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Yahuza Enterprises Trial Balance (Extracts) as at Dec. 31, 1998: Capital N21,000 (Cr); Premises N90,000 (Dr); Debtors N35,000 (Dr); Provisions 1/1/98: Depreciation N9,000, Bad and doubtful debts N1,500. If premises are to be depreciated at 10% on cost and a 5% provision is to be allowed on debtors, the total asset in the balance sheet is
The most convenient cash book used by a petty trader operating in an area where there is no banking facility is
questions.explanation: Without a bank account only cash needs recording, so a single-column cash book suffices.

questions.stem: A general journal contains
options: date, narration, folio, debit and credit
date, narration, folio, debit and purchases
folio, credit, date, debit and sales
debit, credit, narration, date and discount
questions.explanation: The journal has columns for date, particulars/narration, folio, debit and credit.

questions.stem: Which of the following errors will affect the trial balance totals?
options: Posting discount allowed to the debit side of the discount allowed account
Omission of one account from the list when extracting from the ledgers
Failure to post sales of N2,000 and purchases of N2,000 from subsidiary ledgers
Omission of sales of N3,000 and purchase of N2,000
questions.explanation: Leaving out an account balance when listing makes the trial balance totals disagree; the others are either correct or errors that do not upset the agreement.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: An expense account is closed by a debit to
options: an asset account and credit to the expense account
the expense account and a credit to an asset account
profit and loss account and a credit to the expense account
the expense account and a credit to profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Expenses are transferred to profit and loss: debit profit and loss, credit the expense account.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The accounting convention which stipulates that money or goods taken from the business by the owner for personal use should be treated as deductions from capital is
questions.explanation: The business entity concept separates the owner from the business, so drawings reduce the owner's capital.

questions.stem: Use the information: Cost of raw materials consumed N300,600; carriage inwards N6,700; returns of raw materials N10,800; closing stock of raw materials N100,250; manufacturing wages N27,000. What is the cost of the opening raw materials?
questions.explanation: Raw materials consumed = opening stock + carriage inwards − returns − closing stock, so opening = 300,600 − 6,700 + 10,800 + 100,250 = N404,950.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Amin Ltd. Creditors Ledger Control Account (Extracts): Beginning control account balances: debit N32,000; credit N61,000. Purchases during the year: cash N30,000; credit N60,000. Payment to suppliers: cash N13,000; cheque N29,000. Debtors' contra N6,000. The closing control account balance is
questions.explanation: Credits 61,000 + 60,000 = 121,000; debits 32,000 + 13,000 + 29,000 + 6,000 = 80,000; balance = N41,000 (cash purchases do not pass through the control account).

questions.stem: Given: Depreciation of plant and machinery N1,600; factory rent N650; indirect wages N695; general indirect expenses N726; lubricants N1,235; carriage inwards N829; factory power N350; bank charges N612; carriage outwards N2,900. Determine the total factory overhead cost.
questions.explanation: 1,600 + 650 + 695 + 726 + 1,235 + 350 = N5,256; carriage inwards is a materials cost and bank charges and carriage outwards are not factory costs.

questions.stem: Given: Cash book items: paid to suppliers N10,800; expenses paid N6,900; drawings made N900; balances at start N15,750; balances at end N3,870; drawings from bank to shop N1,720. Determine the receipt from debtors.
questions.explanation: Payments + closing balance = 10,800 + 6,900 + 900 + 3,870 = 22,470; less opening 15,750 and bank transfer 1,720 = N5,000 received from debtors.

questions.stem: The items entered in an opening statement of affairs of an enterprise that keeps incomplete records are
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs lists assets and liabilities, such as fixtures and fittings, not income or cash flows.

questions.stem: In a manufacturing company, the total cost of goods produced is equivalent to
questions.explanation: The cost of goods produced is transferred to the trading account where it takes the place of purchases in a trading firm.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Given: Sales Ledger Control Account (Extracts): balance b/f N10,600; total cash payments by debtors N32,275; total credit sales N59,193; discount received N9,700; balance c/f N20,751; discount allowed N2,890. Determine the sales returns.
questions.explanation: Debits 10,600 + 59,193 = 69,793; credits 32,275 + 2,890 + 20,751 = 55,916; sales returns = N13,877 (discount received belongs to the purchases ledger).

questions.stem: A fixed cost is fixed only in relation to
options: a given period of time and a range of activities
a given period of time and the nature of activity
questions.explanation: Fixed costs stay constant only within a given time period and a relevant range of activity.

questions.stem: One of the shortcomings of single entry procedures is that
options: a trial balance is not available
questions.explanation: Without full double entry, a trial balance cannot be extracted to check arithmetical accuracy.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: When a customer's cheque is returned unpaid in a debtors' control accounting system, the treatment will be
options: debit bank, credit customer and credit control account
credit bank, debit customer and debit control account
debit customer, credit control account and credit bank
credit control account, debit bank and debit customer
questions.explanation: A dishonoured cheque reverses the receipt: credit bank, debit the customer's account and debit the sales ledger control account.

questions.stem: Which of the following items does not feature in the balance sheet of a club?
options: Salary arrears paid in the current year
Advance subscription in respect of a coming year
questions.explanation: Salary arrears already paid are settled, so nothing remains to show; the others are assets or liabilities at the year end.

questions.stem: An outright sale of partnership amounts to the
options: compensation of vendors by the purchaser
purchase of rights of a dead partner
change of sharing ratio of vendors
questions.explanation: In an outright sale the purchaser pays the vendor partners the purchase consideration for the business.

questions.stem: Maimalari Ltd had: (i) earnings per share 30k; (iii) par value of each share N1.20; (iv) market price per share N1.50. The company's yield is
questions.explanation: Earnings yield = EPS ÷ market price = 0.30 ÷ 1.50 = 20%.

questions.stem: The partnership deed normally specifies
options: how profits or losses are to be shared
the capital to be contributed annually
how salaries are paid to employees
the profit that should be earned annually
questions.explanation: The deed sets out the profit- and loss-sharing ratio among other partner rights.

questions.stem: When a purchased business is revalued, the effect is that
options: a decrease in the value of assets has no effect on the value of goodwill
an increase in the value of asset is treated as an increase in the value of goodwill
a decrease in the value of asset is treated as a decrease in the value of goodwill
an increase in the value of asset is treated as a decrease in the value of goodwill
questions.explanation: Goodwill = consideration − net assets, so for a given price a higher asset value lowers goodwill.

questions.stem: An item of appropriation in partnership profit and loss account is
questions.explanation: Interest on capital is an appropriation of profit; loan interest and staff salaries are expenses, and drawings go to current accounts.

questions.stem: Rakiya and Joy are in partnership and agreed that 5% interest per annum is to be charged on drawings. The drawings made by both partners in one year (ending 31 December) were: Rakiya, N200 on March 31 and N300 on September 30; Joy, N100 on April 1 and N240 on July 1. The interest on Joy's drawings is

The drawings made by both partners in one year (ending 31 December) were: Rakiya, N200 on March 31 and N300 on September 30; Joy, N100 on April 1 and N240 on July 1. Assuming that Rakiya was not credited with any income during the period, what is her closing current account balance?

Yola Social Club Statement of Account 1999 Financial Year: 31/12/98: subscription in arrears N21,000; subscription in advance N12,000. Receipts during 1999: arrears 1998 N21,000; dues 1999 N48,000; advance 2000 N11,000. The subscription transferable to the income and expenditure account is
questions.explanation: 1999 income = 1999 dues received 48,000 + amount paid in advance in 1998 for 1999 12,000 = N60,000.

questions.stem: The most appropriate basis for apportioning inventory holding cost among departments is to use the value of
questions.explanation: Holding costs accrue over the period, so average stock held by each department is the fairest basis.

questions.stem: Reasons: I. Meet growth and diversification needs. II. Reach out to particular customers or markets. III. Comply with some regulatory directives. IV. Increase employees' income. Which of the reasons above do businesses consider in establishing branches?
questions.explanation: Branches are opened for growth, to reach markets and sometimes on regulatory directive; raising employees' income is not a reason.

questions.stem: The channel through which all government borrowing and domestic lending transactions pass is called
questions.explanation: The national loans fund handles government borrowing and domestic lending.

questions.stem: Given: Floor space: Dept A 400 m^2, Dept B 60 m^2; Machine hours: A 1,200, B 1,400; Turnover: A N36 million, B N64 million; Labour hours: A 1,000, B 1,400. A joint cost of N72 million incurred by the two departments was apportioned N30 million to A and N42 million to B. The basis used for apportionment must have been
questions.explanation: 30 : 42 = 5 : 7, which matches labour hours 1,000 : 1,400.

questions.stem: Recurrent expenditures are expenses for a period not exceeding
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure relates to the current financial year only.

questions.stem: A major benefit derived from the reconciliation of branch and head office books is to
options: determine accurate returns by the branch
ascertain the correct profit or loss on branch activities
enable the branch to keep control over stock
enable the branch to ascertain debtors balance
questions.explanation: Reconciling the current accounts removes in-transit and other differences so the true branch profit or loss is found.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The current growth in the volume of trading and financial dealings in Nigeria is helped by
options: credit as a factor in business
questions.explanation: The availability of credit lets businesses trade beyond their immediate cash, expanding the volume of trading and financial dealings.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: Cost accounting entails provision of information
questions.explanation: Cost accounting provides internal cost information to management for planning, control and decision making.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The main objective of accounting report is to provide information about
questions.explanation: Accounting reports exist to inform users about an entity's economic resources, the claims on them and changes in them.

questions.stem: If liabilities amounted to N12,045, other assets N36,800 and equity N26,896, the cash at hand would be
questions.explanation: Total assets = liabilities + equity = 12,045 + 26,896 = N38,941; cash = 38,941 - 36,800 = N2,141.

questions.stem: Use the information below. Given (N): Fixed assets 85,600; Sales 197,000; Stock 34,300; Salaries and wages 37,000; Purchases 127,700; Share capital 120,000; Creditors 16,050; Motor expenses 10,500; Debtors 25,000. What is the cash balance?
questions.explanation: Credits (sales, capital, creditors) = N333,050; debits without cash = N320,100; cash (debit) = 333,050 - 320,100 = N12,950.

questions.stem: Use the information below. Given (N): Fixed assets 85,600; Sales 197,000; Stock 34,300; Salaries and wages 37,000; Purchases 127,700; Share capital 120,000; Creditors 16,050; Motor expenses 10,500; Debtors 25,000. Determine the total of the trial balance.
questions.explanation: Credit side = 197,000 + 120,000 + 16,050 = N333,050, which the debit side (including cash N12,950) equals.

questions.stem: The accuracy of journalizing is checked by
options: ensuring that debit totals equal credit totals
posting all journal entries to ledger accounts
adding all figures in the debit column
comparing accounts in the ledger against the journals
questions.explanation: Every journal entry has equal debits and credits, so agreement of debit and credit totals checks the journal's arithmetic accuracy.

questions.stem: Hauwa Ltd bought 10 bags of rice for N500 each. The company was given 5% and 12% trade and cash discounts respectively. What will be recorded as discount received in the company's book?
questions.explanation: Trade discount is not recorded: 5,000 less 5% = N4,750; cash discount received = 12% of 4,750 = N570.

questions.explanation: Substance over form requires transactions to be recorded according to their economic reality rather than their legal form.

questions.explanation: Contra entries between the cash and bank columns are completed within the same book (the cash book), on opposite sides.

questions.stem: Given: Capital N1 000; Liabilities N500; Assets N1 500. The accounting equation can be expressed as
questions.explanation: Capital + Liabilities = Assets: N1,000 + N500 = N1,500.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The recording phase of accounting is known as
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping is the recording phase of accounting; accounting goes on to summarise, analyse and interpret.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Motor Vehicle Account as at 31st December, 2001: Debit: Jan. 1, cost N1,950 000; Dec. 31, Addition N400 000. Credit: Jan. 1, Depreciation N1,360 000; June 30, Sales proceeds N700 000. The vehicle sold was purchased on January 1, 1998 at a cost of N1,000 000 and had depreciated at 25% on cost. Assuming that depreciation is charged on the addition of the year at the rate of 15% on reducing balance, what should be the net book value of the vehicle as at 31st December 2003?
questions.explanation: The addition (N400,000 on 31 Dec 2001) is depreciated for 2002 and 2003 at 15% reducing balance: 400,000 x 0.85 x 0.85 = N289,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given: I. Order of permanence II. Order of liquidity III. Vertical order IV. Horizontal order. The orders in which a balance sheet asset is arranged are
questions.explanation: Balance sheet assets are listed either in order of permanence or in order of liquidity (the paper misprints "permanence" as "performance"); vertical and horizontal are formats, not orders.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Provision for discount allowed can be recorded as a debit to
options: the profit and loss account and a credit to provision for discount allowed
provision for discount allowed and a credit to the profit and loss account
discount allowed and a credit to the profit and loss account
expenses and a credit to customers’ account
questions.explanation: Creating a provision for discount allowed charges profit and loss (debit) and credits the provision account.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Feb. 1 Purchased 400 units at N1.00 each; Feb. 5 Purchased 200 units at N2.00 each; Feb. 10 Purchased 200 units at N3.00 each; Feb. 15 Issued 320 units; Feb. 20 Purchased 200 units at N4.00 each; Feb. 25 Issued 120 units. Calculate the price per unit of closing stock using the periodic weighted average method.
questions.explanation: Periodic weighted average = total cost / total units purchased = (400 + 400 + 600 + 800) / 1,000 = N2.20.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Purchases ledger control account: Debit side: Discount received N1,000; Bills payable N1,500; Cash paid to suppliers N8,000; Returns outwards N3,000; Balance c/d ?. Credit side: Balance b/d N2,900; Credit purchases ?; Bills payable dishonoured N1,600; Dishonoured cheques N2,000. Credit purchases are always put at 150% of the total cash paid to suppliers. Calculate the closing balance of the ledger account
questions.explanation: Credit purchases = 150% x 8,000 = 12,000. Credit total = 2,900 + 12,000 + 1,600 + 2,000 = 18,500; debits before the balance = 13,500, so balance c/d = N5,000.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Purchases ledger control account: Debit side: Discount received N1,000; Bills payable N1,500; Cash paid to suppliers N8,000; Returns outwards N3,000; Balance c/d ?. Credit side: Balance b/d N2,900; Credit purchases ?; Bills payable dishonoured N1,600; Dishonoured cheques N2,000. Credit purchases are always put at 150% of the total cash paid to suppliers. Determine the credit purchases
questions.explanation: Credit purchases = 150% of cash paid to suppliers = 1.5 x N8,000 = N12,000.

questions.stem: The stock valuation data is important because it enables management to
options: determine the cost of stock at the end of business
determine the cost of stock at the beginning of business
determine the total cost of goods purchased
questions.explanation: Stock valuation establishes the value of closing stock, needed for cost of sales and the balance sheet.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: During the year ended 31st December 2001, Nuju Enterprises paid rent as follows: Jan. 20 N24 000 for a period of 4 months; May 16 N30 000 for a period of 5 months; Oct. 15 N36 000 for a period of 6 months. What is the overpaid portion of the rent?
questions.explanation: Rent is N6,000 a month; the October payment covers October to March, so 3 months (Jan-Mar 2002) x N6,000 = N18,000 is prepaid.

questions.stem: Advertising expenses incurred on a product in a business organization should be charged to
questions.explanation: Advertising is a selling expense, so it is charged to the sales department.

questions.stem: Four broad classifications of overheads are
questions.explanation: Overheads are classified as production, administration, selling and distribution; materials and wages are direct costs.

questions.stem: Given: Cost of raw material issued to production N37,000; Opening stock of raw material N2,000; Purchases of raw material N38,000; Wages N5,000. What is the closing stock of raw material?
questions.explanation: Closing stock = opening + purchases - issued = 2,000 + 38,000 - 37,000 = N3,000.

questions.stem: PQ Manufacturing Company: Raw materials (1/1/2001) N3,500; Raw materials (31/12/2001) N4,900; Purchase of raw materials N56,000; Salary N63,000; Wages N148,050; Factory lighting N3,080; Plant depreciation N2,800; Factory insurance N2,170. The overhead cost is
questions.explanation: Overheads = salary 63,000 + factory lighting 3,080 + plant depreciation 2,800 + factory insurance 2,170 = N71,050 (wages are direct labour).

questions.stem: PQ Manufacturing Company: Raw materials (1/1/2001) N3,500; Raw materials (31/12/2001) N4,900; Purchase of raw materials N56,000; Salary N63,000; Wages N148,050; Factory lighting N3,080; Plant depreciation N2,800; Factory insurance N2,170. The company consumed raw materials worth
questions.explanation: Raw materials consumed = 3,500 + 56,000 - 4,900 = N54,600.

questions.stem: A company has two departments X and Y. Y transferred goods to X at a profit margin of 25%. N10 000 worth of goods was not sold at the end of the accounting period. How much is the unrealized profit?
questions.explanation: A 25% margin is profit as a percentage of the transfer price: 25% x N10,000 = N2,500 unrealised profit.

questions.stem: A company has departments M and N. The expense incurred wholly in M is N5 000. General expenses incurred amount to N25 000. Expenses are apportioned in the ratio 2:3 for departments M and N respectively. What is N’s share of the expenses?
questions.explanation: Only the general expenses are shared: 3/5 x N25,000 = N15,000; the N5,000 belongs wholly to M.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Total sales of tickets N300 000; Amount received from the sales N260 000; Cash purchase of the club house N100 000; Credit purchase of equipment N60 000; Electricity bill paid N5 000; Salaries owed N2 000. What is the receipts and payments account balance?
questions.explanation: Cash received 260,000 less cash paid (club house 100,000 + electricity 5,000) = N155,000; credit and owed items are not cash.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Total sales of tickets N300 000; Amount received from the sales N260 000; Cash purchase of the club house N100 000; Credit purchase of equipment N60 000; Electricity bill paid N5 000; Salaries owed N2 000. What is the balance of the income and expenditure account?
questions.explanation: Income earned from ticket sales 300,000 less revenue expenses (electricity 5,000 + salaries owed 2,000) = N293,000; the club house and equipment are capital items.

questions.stem: The first step in converting a single entry to a double entry system of bookkeeping is to prepare a
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs is prepared first to find the opening capital before the double entry accounts are built up.

questions.stem: Emeka Enterprises Statement of Affairs at start: Assets: Cash N70 000; Inventory N58 000; Machines N100 000. Liabilities: Creditors N85 000; Bank Loan N60 000. What is the capital at start?
questions.explanation: Capital = assets 228,000 - liabilities 145,000 = N83,000.

questions.stem: Receipts and payments account is the summary of
questions.explanation: A receipts and payments account summarises the cash book of a not-for-profit organisation.

questions.stem: Given: Total debtors b/d 31/12/99 N25 000; Cheques received from debtors N225 000; Total debtors c/d 31/12/00 N15 000. Determine the sales figure.
questions.explanation: Credit sales = closing debtors + receipts - opening debtors = 15,000 + 225,000 - 25,000 = N215,000.

questions.stem: Which of these is a capital expenditure warrant?
questions.explanation: The Development Fund General Warrant authorises the release of funds for capital expenditure.

questions.stem: For the purpose of conversion of a partnership to a company, a total purchase consideration of N3.6m was paid. If 30% of the purchase consideration was in cash and the rest by 50k shares, how many shares were issued?

Use the information below (branch): Goods from head office N13,400; Returns to head office N118; Rates and insurance paid N188; Wages paid N913; Cash remitted to head office N16,625; Stock at 1/1/2000 N1,875; Rent paid N325; Stock at 31/12/2000 N1,975; Sundry expenses N200. The profit realized from the trade is
questions.explanation: Sales (cash remitted) 16,625 - cost of sales (1,875 + 13,400 - 118 - 1,975 = 13,182) = 3,443 gross profit; less expenses 1,626 = N1,817.

questions.stem: Use the information below (branch): Goods from head office N13,400; Returns to head office N118; Rates and insurance paid N188; Wages paid N913; Cash remitted to head office N16,625; Stock at 1/1/2000 N1,875; Rent paid N325; Stock at 31/12/2000 N1,975; Sundry expenses N200. What is the total expenses?
questions.explanation: Expenses = rates and insurance 188 + wages 913 + rent 325 + sundry 200 = N1,626.

questions.stem: The amount of each invoiced goods sent to the branch is debited to
options: branch expense account and credited to branch debtors’ account
branch stock account and credited to the goods sent to branch account
branch debtors’ account and credited to branch expense account
goods sent to branch account and credited to branch expense account
questions.explanation: Goods sent to a branch: debit branch stock account, credit goods sent to branch account.

questions.stem: ZEBRA PLC Balance sheet as at 31st March, 2002: Capital N100 000; Current liabilities: Creditors N30 000; total N130 000. Fixed assets: Land and buildings N50,000; Furniture N10,000 (N60,000). Current assets: Stock N30,000; Debtors N30,000; Cash N10,000 (N70,000); total N130,000. The business was acquired on 1st April, 2002 at a purchase consideration of N120 000 by SOZ. All assets and liabilities were taken over except the cash. To open the new firm’s bank account, additional N20,000 was paid into the bank. The goodwill on purchase is
Gross profit in the branch adjustment account is transferred to the branch
questions.explanation: The gross profit shown by the branch adjustment (mark-up) account is transferred to the branch profit and loss account.

questions.stem: Mamza Nigeria Limited issued 20 000 ordinary shares of N1.50 per share. On 2nd July 2002, 1 500 ordinary shares were fully subscribed for and their monies received as follows: On application N0.40; On allotment N0.20; First call (including premium of N0.50) N0.70. The last and final call was yet to be made. What is the balance of the ordinary share capital account after the first call was received?
questions.explanation: Share capital is credited with the nominal part only: 0.40 + 0.20 + (0.70 - 0.50) = N0.80 per share x 1,500 = N1,200; the premium goes to share premium account.

questions.topic: Nature and Significance of Book keeping and Accounting
questions.stem: The accounting principle that is applied to check arbitrary actions on the part of accountants is
questions.explanation: Objectivity requires entries to be based on verifiable evidence rather than the personal judgement of the accountant.

questions.stem: The loss of equipment in a fire disaster results in
options: an increase in liabilities and assets
a decrease in assets and capital
an increase in liabilities and a decrease in assets
questions.explanation: Equipment (an asset) is lost and the loss reduces capital, so both assets and capital fall.

questions.stem: The rule of accounting equation requires that account payable should be placed under
questions.explanation: Accounts payable are amounts owed to creditors, i.e. liabilities.

questions.stem: Cash Book: Debit: Capital N6 600; Sales N3 000; Debtors N2 500. Credit: Purchases N3,500; Stationery N1,300; Wages N2 700. The owner wishes to maintain an amount equal to 1/3 of capital as drawings. The amount withdrawn is
questions.explanation: Drawings = 1/3 x N6,600 = N2,200.

questions.stem: Cash Book: Debit: Capital N6 600; Sales N3 000; Debtors N2 500. Credit: Purchases N3,500; Stationery N1,300; Wages N2 700. The owner wishes to maintain an amount equal to 1/3 of capital as drawings. The cash book closing balance will be
A debit in the suspense account will appear in the balance sheet as
questions.explanation: A debit balance on suspense account is shown among current assets until the errors are found.

questions.stem: The recipient whose name appears on cheque is called a
questions.explanation: The payee is the person named on the cheque to receive payment; the drawer writes it and the drawee is the bank.

questions.stem: The imprest account is subsidiary to the
questions.explanation: The petty cash (imprest) book is a subsidiary of the main cash book.

questions.stem: The three-column cash book differs from the two-column cash book in
questions.explanation: The three-column cash book adds a discount column to the cash and bank columns.

questions.stem: Zakari started business in January 2000. He bought a shop costing N54,000 and stock worth N7,600. Profit for the year amounted to N22,100. His closing capital was N73,800. Zakari’s personal drawings amounted to
questions.explanation: Opening capital 61,600 + profit 22,100 - drawings = 73,800, so drawings = N9,900.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: The balance on the provision for depreciation account is
options: added to fixed assets on the balance sheet
deducted from fixed assets on the balance sheet
deducted from the profit and loss account
added to the current liabilities of the account
questions.explanation: Accumulated depreciation is deducted from the cost of fixed assets to give net book value.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given: Rates paid during the year amount to N2,250 at N125 per month and N1,035 was paid for electricity in the same period at N115 per month. Determine the amount of prepaid rates
questions.explanation: Rates for the year = 12 x 125 = 1,500; N2,250 was paid, so N750 is prepaid.

questions.stem: Use the information below: May 2 Receipt 80 units @ N3.00; May 10 Receipt 50 units @ N3.20; May 17 Issued 20 units; May 25 Issued 60 units; May 31 Receipt 20 units @ N2.90. What is the value of raw materials issued on May 17th based on the LIFO method?
questions.explanation: Under LIFO the 20 units come from the latest receipt (May 10 at N3.20): 20 x 3.20 = N64.

questions.stem: Use the information below: May 2 Receipt 80 units @ N3.00; May 10 Receipt 50 units @ N3.20; May 17 Issued 20 units; May 25 Issued 60 units; May 31 Receipt 20 units @ N2.90. Based on the FIFO method of valuation, the total cost of raw materials issued is
questions.explanation: FIFO: the 80 units issued all come from the first batch of 80 at N3.00 = N240.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Where closing stock is undervalued, the effect is
questions.explanation: Lower closing stock raises cost of sales, so gross profit falls.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Use the information below: Opening balance N10,640; Purchases N26,912; Returns inwards N492; Returns outwards N810; Cash discount received N1,348; Cash discount allowed N1,560; Cash paid to suppliers N20,808. At the year-end, the purchases ledger showed a debit balance of N108. The total on the debit side of the purchase ledger control account will be:
questions.explanation: Debit entries: returns outwards 810 + discount received 1,348 + cash paid 20,808 = N22,966 (returns inwards and discount allowed belong to the sales ledger).

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: Use the information below: Opening balance N10,640; Purchases N26,912; Returns inwards N492; Returns outwards N810; Cash discount received N1,348; Cash discount allowed N1,560; Cash paid to suppliers N20,808. At the year-end, the purchases ledger showed a debit balance of N108. The balancing figure in the purchases ledger control account is
questions.explanation: Credits: 10,640 + 26,912 + debit balance c/d 108 = 37,660; less debit entries 22,966 = closing credit balance N14,694.

questions.topic: Control Accounts and Self balancing ledger
questions.stem: In a sales ledger, contra entry is found on the
options: debit side of the debtors’ control account
debit side of the creditors’ control account
credit side of the debtors’ control account
credit side of the creditors’ control account
questions.explanation: A set-off (contra) reduces the amount owed by debtors, so it is credited in the sales ledger (debtors) control account.

questions.stem: The beginning and ending accounts receivable balances were N20,000 and N30,000 respectively. The collection from customers during the period was N70,000. What was the total sale on account?
questions.explanation: Credit sales = closing 30,000 + collections 70,000 - opening 20,000 = N80,000.

questions.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
questions.stem: Given: General expenses account: Paid by cheque N671; Paid by cash N70; Accrued b/f N65; Accrued c/f N115. Determine how much to be charged to profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Charge = payments 741 - accrual b/f 65 + accrual c/f 115 = N791.

questions.stem: In converting single entry to final account, the balancing figures on the income and expenses accounts are transferred to the
questions.explanation: The reconstructed income and expense accounts give the figures for the profit and loss account.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Beginning inventory ?; Purchases ?; Ending inventory N4,800; Sales N12,800; Wages N1,040; Gross profit N5,900. The beginning inventory was estimated at 80% of sales. Determine the amount for the beginning inventory
questions.explanation: Beginning inventory = 80% x N12,800 = N10,240.

questions.stem: Cost classification in relation to changes is determined by the level of
questions.explanation: Classifying costs as fixed, variable or semi-variable depends on how they change with the level of activity.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Materials consumed N16,600; Direct cost N5,400; Factory rent N2,300; Factory lighting N1,200. Cost of production to be transferred at cost plus 20% mark-up. The gross profit on manufacture is

Use the information below: Materials consumed N16,600; Direct cost N5,400; Factory rent N2,300; Factory lighting N1,200. Cost of production to be transferred at cost plus 20% mark-up. The market value of goods produced is
questions.explanation: Market value = cost of production 25,500 x 1.2 = N30,600.

questions.stem: On January 1, 2000, a club’s assets and liabilities were as follows: Club house N8000; Subscription in arrears N300; Cash N1000; Wages owed N100. The club has 50 members and annual subscription is N100 per member. Subscription received is N4,000 and this includes 1999 arrears of N200. The accumulated fund is
questions.explanation: Accumulated fund = assets (8,000 + 300 + 1,000) - liabilities 100 = N9,200.

questions.stem: Where the debit side of the income and expenditure account is higher than the credit side, the difference is a
questions.explanation: Expenditure exceeding income in an income and expenditure account gives a deficit.

questions.stem: In the balance sheet of a not-for profit making organization, subscription paid in advance is regarded as a
questions.explanation: Subscriptions received in advance are owed to members as future services, so they are a current liability.

questions.stem: A rapidly growing business organisation with multiple units that is interested in comparing the performances and weakness of each unit should adopt
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts show the results of each unit separately for comparison.

questions.stem: Use the information below: Dept. S / Dept. T / Total: Gross profit b/d 6,000 / 4,000 / 10,000; Less: salaries & wages 1,800 / 1,200 / 3,000; Electricity ? / ? / 2,000; Depreciation 60 / ? / 1,000; Net profit c/d ? / 1,600 / 4,000. What is the net profit by department S?
questions.explanation: Total net profit 4,000 - department T net profit 1,600 = N2,400 for S.

questions.stem: How are credit sales by a department treated?
options: the same way as normal debtors’ transactions
in a different way from normal debtors’ transactions
as an addition to the sales manager’s account
as an addition to the production manager’s account
questions.explanation: Departmental credit sales are recorded like any other credit sales to debtors.

questions.stem: Discounts granted to branch customers are treated as a debit to branch
options: stock account and a credit to branch debtors’ account
discount account and a credit to branch bank account
stock account and a credit to branch bank account
discount account and a credit to branch debtors’ account
questions.explanation: Discount allowed reduces what branch debtors owe: debit branch discount account, credit branch debtors account.

questions.stem: On dissolution, the final distribution of cash to partners is based on
questions.explanation: After the assets are realised and liabilities paid, the remaining cash is paid out according to the partners’ capital account balances.

questions.stem: Jumoke and Kunle have an original investment of N25,000 and N15,000 respectively in a partnership. The articles of partnership provide 3% interest on capital and salaries of N1,500 and N1,000 respectively for the parties. The profit & loss are to be shared in the ratio 3:2. Miscellaneous expenses of N2,500 were incurred with gross profit of N6,500 during the financial year. What is Kunle’s share of the profit?
questions.explanation: Net profit 4,000 - interest on capital (750 + 450) - salaries 2,500 = 300 residual; Kunle gets 2/5 x 300 = N120.

questions.stem: When a new partner is admitted to a partnership there is a need to revalue the
options: capital and liabilities of the business
assets and capital of the business
assets and liabilities of the business
questions.explanation: On admission, assets and liabilities are revalued so that existing partners get the gains or losses up to that date.

questions.stem: The accounting entry to record the premium on goodwill is to debit
options: cash and credit old partners’ capital
questions.explanation: A premium for goodwill paid in cash by the new partner is debited to cash and credited to the old partners’ capital accounts.

questions.stem: The expenses incurred in promoting a company are:
questions.explanation: Costs of forming and promoting a company are called preliminary (formation) expenses.

questions.stem: Given: Share capital (issued): 600,000 10% preference shares of N0.50 each -; 600,000 ordinary shares of N1 each N500,000; Capital reserves N250,000; Revenue reserves N207,000; Long-term liabilities N400,000; Total N1,357,000. The value of the owner’s equity is
questions.explanation: Owners’ equity = issued share capital 500,000 + capital reserves 250,000 + revenue reserves 207,000 = N957,000 (long-term liabilities excluded).

questions.stem: Share premium is an example of
questions.explanation: Share premium is a statutory capital reserve, not available for cash dividends.

questions.stem: The budget statement presented to the legislature by the Chief Executive is called
questions.explanation: The executive presents the budget to the legislature as an Appropriation Bill; once passed it becomes an Appropriation Act.

questions.stem: The statement of assets and liabilities in the public sector can be described as the
options: income and expenditure account of government
questions.explanation: The statement of assets and liabilities is the government’s equivalent of a balance sheet.
